For years, residents of a Southern California beach town could walk a mile along a stretch of cream-colored sand while ocean waves lapped at their feet. That journey has now been cut short.
San Clemente, recognized for nearly a century as a "Spanish village by the sea," is losing its shoreline to erosion. Rising seas and crashing waves have bisected the city's picturesque North Beach, while eroding bluffs threaten waterfront homes and have repeatedly forced the closure of a passenger train route considered the second busiest in the country.
It is one of numerous California coastal communities confronting the effects of sea level rise. Nearly a decade ago, scientists forecast that more than half of Southern California’s beaches could significantly erode by 2100, radically altering how people live and recreate along the state’s famed coast.
"The constant pressure is sea level rise," said Sean Vitousek, research oceanographer with the U.S. Geological Survey. "It is going to keep rising, and rising, and the beaches will retreat landward."
Following years of erosion, California is preparing for flooding and landslides ahead of this year’s expected super El Niño, a temporary warming in parts of the equatorial Pacific that warps weather worldwide. Already this year, seawater flooded residences in Long Beach near Los Angeles during a hurricane-driven storm surge, and the town of Pacifica south of San Francisco closed its cracked concrete pier. A recent study indicated that El Niño events are strengthening due to human-caused climate change.
In San Clemente, a town of 62,000 people, urban development has restricted the flow of sediment that historically replenished local beaches, while warmer waters drive waves higher and further ashore. The challenge has led residents of the largely Republican city to consider taxing themselves for beach restoration. A measure adding a 1% sales tax to fund wildfire protection and sand replenishment is on the November ballot.
Crumbling hillsides disrupt seaside rail
Over the past five years, the rail line operating along the coast for more than a century has faced recurring closures due to encroaching surf on one side and fragile bluffs on the other. The 7-mile (11-kilometer) segment belongs to a 351-mile (565-kilometer) passenger rail corridor connecting San Diego with Los Angeles County's major port complex and San Luis Obispo. It is also used by freight and the military.
Transportation officials have reinforced the tracks to ensure passenger safety by laying down rock. But as waves slam against the rocks, they sweep more sand offshore and accelerate erosion that will eventually threaten the rail line again.
Locals say the erosion is dramatically altering their community.
"We've lost our walkable beach," said Cameron Cosgrove, a San Clemente resident who wrote the tax measure. "It used to be you could come to North Beach, walk the beach trail, or on the beach to the pier and actually all the way down to the south end of town. Can’t do either anymore."
City and transit officials agree more sand is needed and note that coastal communities, including surf hub Huntington Beach, have nourished their beaches for years. Opponents of the measure want sand — but not the tax — and argue San Clemente should work with other communities on a regional approach.
"Fighting Mother Nature is very expensive," said City Councilman Zhen Wu, who opposes the measure.
City Manager Andy Hall said San Clemente faces a sand deficit of about 3 million cubic yards. Getting that much sand to the beach is no easy task, he said, adding that trucking it would require 300,000 trips.
Darrell Johnson, chief executive of the Orange County Transportation Authority, said a challenge has been getting state permits for more sand. He hopes California's recent emergency declaration ahead of El Niño will speed up the process. In the long run, Johnson said officials will study moving trains inland — an idea previously deemed too costly. A third option is to halt the line, he said.
"If we can’t figure out how to shore up properly in a way that is long-term in nature, and we can't figure out how to relocate, I think that is a question that’s going to have to be asked," Johnson said. "'What happens to passenger rail? What happens to freight?'"
More sand will also shape wave breaks
Further south, transportation officials have been working to stabilize coastal bluffs to shore up the rail line in the community of Del Mar. The plan is to eventually move the tracks, but officials have not decided where.
Charlie Fox, a 56-year-old San Clemente resident and marine meteorologist, said sand provides a critical buffer between whatever structures — train tracks, homes, lifeguard headquarters — are built along the coast. The lifelong surfer said sand also helps waves roll gently onshore, creating a steady wave break for surfing.
On a recent morning, surfers bobbed in the water off North Beach, not far from the rocky structure shoring up the train tracks by the sea.
"When you see those rocks, that's them attempting to fight the ocean," Fox said. "That is a futile endeavor."
"The ocean wins," he added. "Ocean always eventually wins."

Nor'easter storm brings coastal flooding, as New York and New Jersey declare emergency
- Published
Tens of millions of people across the north-eastern US are in the path of a powerful storm this weekend, which has already brought coastal flooding, power outages, travel chaos and cancelled stadium events.
Peaking on Saturday, the so-called nor'easter will "bring dangerous coastal flooding and beach conditions, strong winds, and heavy rainfall" to areas including New York City and Boston, the US National Weather Service (NWS) said.
States of emergency have been declared in New York and New Jersey, the latter of which is already facing a coastal deluge in some areas. Rain and strong winds are forecast from Virginia to Maine.
Ed Sheeran's much-awaited Boston concert was among events called off.
The nor'easter is already causing widespread power outages. Nearly 150,000 households have so far lost electricity, according to poweroutageus.
The Federal Aviation Administration recommended flyers check with airlines about their flight status. More than 1,100 flights have been delayed and another 400 grounded, according to FlightAware.
Saturday's full moon is projected to worsen coastal inundations. Streets and homes were flooded on Saturday in the coastal New Jersey communities of Surf City and Manasquan.
"I urge all New Jerseyans to take this storm seriously, stay alert, and follow local guidance," Governor Mikie Sherrill said.
NWS said in its alert: "Prepare immediately for significant inundation in low-lying areas near the shore, including roads underwater and impacts to homes and businesses."
In New York, officials are warning of wind gusts of up to 55mph (86km/h) throughout the weekend, leading to downed trees and power outages.
"Don't travel if you don't have to," Mayor Zohran Mamdani told residents in a video message. "Do not drive or walk through floodwater."
In the Boston area, the Red Sox moved their weekend series against the Chicago Cubs from Sunday afternoon game to next Friday.
A professional football match between Red Bull New York and St Louis City SC was also cancelled.
Nor is the Global Citizen Festival concert in New York City's Central Park, which was to be headlined by Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and John Legend, going ahead.
Sheeran's concert at the Gillette Stadium in the Boston-area was cancelled for safety reasons, the venue said.

BYD says its new solid-state EV battery tech is nearly ready for the open road
The Chinese company is one of several car makers expected to adopt solid-state batteries in the next few years.
Switching from lithium-ion to solid-state batteries promises to extend the range and charging speeds of electric vehicles, and Chinese car maker BYD believes it's in a "leading position" to commercialize the technology. BYD's Executive Vice President Stella Li shared the claim in a recent interview with Carwow's Spanish outlet, alongside the news that BYD would release its first car with a solid-state battery in 2027.
"Talking about solid-state batteries, BYD is in the leading position," Li said. "We're in the leading position for commercialization and technology. So to prove that, next year, we have one model that will be the first one with that technology."
Li's comments further confirm plans shared by Sun Huajun, the Chief Technology Officer of BYD's battery subsidiary FinDreams, at a battery conference in February 2025. At the time, Sun said BYD would offer its first demonstration and installation of solid-state batteries in 2027 before the technology enters mass production around 2030, CarNewsChina reports. While that means people will be able to buy cars with the company's sulfide solid-state batteries, that doesn't mean its traditional lithium batteries will be phased out, BYD Chief Scientist Lian Yubo shared at the same conference. "Solid-state batteries will be mainly used in high-end models, empowering each other with lithium iron phosphate batteries, and used in vehicles of different levels," Lian said.
In comparison to lithium-ion batteries, which move ions between positive and negative terminals through a liquid solution of dissolved lithium salts, solid-state batteries replace the liquid with solid electrolytes made from oxides, polymers or sulfides (the kind BYD is developing). Solid electrolytes give solid-state batteries higher energy density, which opens up the possibility of smaller, lighter batteries and a longer range on a single charge. Solid-state batteries are also theoretically safer because they're far less prone to catching fire and they're able to operate at extreme temperatures, an issue current lithium-ion batteries struggle with.
The problem with using the battery technology as it exists now is cost, which is why BYD suggests you'll see its solid-state batteries on more expensive models first, like possibly a future version of its Denza Z. The company is one of several car makers planning to ship a vehicle with solid-state batteries in the next few years. For example, Toyota committed to offering cars with solid-state batteries by 2027 or 2028; Mercedes-Benz began testing a solid-state EQS model and shared that it would ship the technology before the end of the decade; and Stellantis began road testing a solid-state Dodge Charger in 2026. Earlier this year, Honda struck up a new partnership with QuantumScape to develop solid-state batteries it hopes will help it reach carbon neutrality by 2050. The potential for solid-state battery technology is exciting, but most car makers are only in the first leg of the race.

An at-home cat or dog DNA test kit promises to give pet owners clarity on a heap of important health data, like breed ancestry, blood type, and health risks. To access this info, owners just swab the inside of their pet’s mouth, seal the sample in a prepaid-postage envelope, and wait (for up to five weeks) for results to be sent to their inbox. Each company has a testing lab, and the results live in your online account, where they can be downloaded and even shared with your vet.
But because of several factors, such as sample size and comparison, these tests often give dramatically different results for things like genetic ancestry and breed traits (more on that below).
I tested several at-home DNA test kits, including two of the most popular kits—Basepaws ($104) and Wisdom Panel ($97)—on my two adult cats and talked to several animal experts to get insights into these tests—and whether they are worth your money, given the large disparity in results. Think of this as the WIRED guide to the increasingly popular at-home pet DNA test.
Table of Contents
Be sure to check out our related guides, like the Best Automatic Cat Feeders, Best Automatic Litter Boxes, Best Automatic Cat Fountains, and Best Dog Accessories.
Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.
Easiest Interface
|  | Breed | Health Test | Trait Test | Blood Type/Transfusion Risk | Oral Health Report | Family Tree | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wisdom Panel (Cat) | Screens for 70+ breeds and populations | Tests for 45+ genetic health conditions | Test for 25+ physical traits | Yes | No | Yes | 
In my research, I've found that people widely consider Wisdom Panel the most trusted at-home pet DNA test kit (along with dog-only Embark, which former WIRED reviewer Julia Forbes tested below).
Wisdom Panel offers several kits for dogs (listed below) but only one test for cats. It can identify more than 70 breeds, includes 45 health tests, determines blood type, and screens for more than 25 traits. It even provides a genetic consult for “at-risk” health findings and shows what the pet's family tree might look like based on DNA results. I especially liked that it tests for the most common conditions seen in cats or dogs with a similar breed makeup to your pet (based on the DNA sample), including important markers like drug sensitivity, immune deficiency, and bleeding disorders. It also identified the cat’s blood type (both of my cats were A) and transfusion risk (both were moderate).
The results arrived live online in my Wisdom Panel account within three weeks of mailing them. I really appreciated the interface, which was organized into clickable tabs that made the information easier to access and navigate. Plus, based on appearance alone, my cat Clover's DNA results seemed most accurate with this test (below). I also tested my run-of-the-mill gray tabby cat, Basil, but on all tests—including Wisdom Panel—he was almost entirely labeled as an “American domestic cat” and “polycat/domestic shorthair." That's basically the mutt final boss, a result of many generations of mixed breeding among different cat types, where ancestry and origin are almost impossible to determine.
| Clover’s Wisdom Panel Results | 
|---|
| American domestic cat: 51 percent | 
| Highlander: 13 percent | 
| Norwegian Forest Cat: 13 percent | 
| Siamese and Oriental: 13 percent | 
| LaPerm: 10 percent | 
Most In-Depth Results
|  | Breed | Health Test | Trait Test | Blood Type/Transfusion Risk | Oral Health Report | Family Tree | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Basepaws (Cat) | Tests against 21 breeds | Tests for 64 genetic health markers | Tests for 50 genetic trait markers | Yes | Yes | No | 
WIRED reviewed Basepaws over half a decade ago, and a lot has changed since then. Basepaws offers a single breed and health test for cats that identifies up to 21 breeds, 64 genetic health markers, 50 genetic trait markers, blood type, and oral health. The wait time for results is five weeks, and when I first sent my cat Basil's test in, they couldn't extract enough DNA, so I had to send another sample and wait another five weeks. Rather than an easily digestible interactive screen with information like Wisdom Panel, Basepaws gives you essentially a mini book PDF to scroll through to find information. It feels more in-depth than Wisdom Panel, but it is also harder to disseminate the large pile of information.
Basepaws tests genes for markers associated with disorders in musculoskeletal and connective tissue; eyes; metabolic, autoimmune, and endocrine systems; blood; and more. Both of my cats, Clover and Basil, were cleared of any genes that would mark them as potential carriers of genetic diseases. It also identified blood type and transfusion risk, which were A and moderate (the same results I got with Wisdom Panel’s test).
Basepaws tests for oral health by comparing against an oral microbiome database. In this regard, Basepaws wins out. Dental health is a major concern for me, and I love that Basepaws screens for it and provides an oral health report (I have since started brushing my cats' teeth). My cat Basil was at high risk for all dental markers like halitosis, tooth resorption, and periodontal disease. Basepaws developed a health plan for him: “Adopt a daily oral health care routine, consider supplementing Basil’s routine with products accepted by the Veterinary Oral Health Council, and schedule an appointment with your veterinarian in the next month.” Although I was alarmed by the results, I appreciated that Basepaws provided recommended next steps so I could develop a plan of action for care. And it’s important to remember that these results don’t necessarily mean a pet is guaranteed to develop the disease.
"These can be a helpful flag for your veterinarian to keep an eye on [...] but do not necessarily mean aggressive testing is needed at that moment,” says Jamie Richardson, head of veterinary medicine at Small Door Veterinary. “DNA tests are tools to support—not replace—veterinary care.”
Some of the other Basepaws results, particularly the genetic and physical markers, seem off. Like Wisdom Panel, white calico Clover was marked as “likely” to be black in color, and none of the ancestral DNA breeds matched across tests for Clover.

| Maine coon: 12.27 percent | 
| Ragdoll: 11.8 percent | 
| Persian: 6.99 percent | 
| Siberian: 6.2 percent |

Another Cat DNA Test Kit I Tested

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Koko Genetics | Yes; tests against an unspecified number | Tests for 55 genetic health markers | Tests for 40 traits | No | No | Yes | 
Koko Genetics was a new name to me, but it offers a similar service to the two major brands above, with tests for both cats and dogs in “starter” basic and “advanced” kits. I tested the latter, which provides additional health insights by screening for genetic disorders or abnormalities. The process is exactly the same as with the other kits, where you swab your cat's mouth, register your kit online, and mail the results. The Koko Genetics interface wouldn't allow me to register two kits with different cats under the same login/username, so I had to create two separate accounts with two different emails, which was a slight pain. The results also took surprisingly long—it took over five weeks from mailing to being acknowledged as received, and an additional five weeks to get results.
This interface was the least user-friendly of all I tested, and many of the default options were in Spanish with no English options. The site where you access results is a little bare-bones, with additional information available if you click the tab. I found that much of the health trait info was scientific jargon, and I had to do further research to understand it. Clover was flagged as having a copy of the Acute Intermittent Porphyria (Variant 3) gene mutation, which can cause discolored teeth and urine and may lead to other health problems. Luckily, Clover has just one copy of the mutation and will not develop the disease, but she can transmit the mutation to her offspring. (She's spayed, so that is not a potential issue.) Wisdom Panel also tests for this, and she was not flagged as carrying it in that test.
Both cats were negative for all physical traits except black coat (which neither has), and I didn't find the info really helpful or interesting. There's also a family tree option, like Wisdom Panel's, where you can see what the previous generations' breed or coloring might've been.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Embark Dog | Tests against over 400 breeds | No | No; results for likely personality traits rather than physical | No | No | Yes | 
One of my family’s favorite pastimes is placing low-stakes bets on the breeds that make up our beloved rescue dogs. Usually we’re wildly off with our estimates. For my dog Randy, all we knew was that he was a Chihuahua mix. The Embark DNA kit is the dog equivalent of Ancestry DNA for humans, given how detailed it is. The test kit uses a saliva sample, and you ship it off for processing. Within three weeks, we found out Randy had quite the cocker spaniel lineage, with show-dog cousins across the country (Princess Elysia of Eagle’s Wings’ parents, if you’re reading this, hello!).
The Embark app gives detailed breakdowns of behavioral, health, and longevity insights for the breeds that make up your pup. His personality analysis shows he’s closely aligned with his cocker spaniel roots, always on the lookout (check), sometimes high-energy (check), and rarely independent (spot on). —Julia Forbes
The kits below are also specifically for dogs from Basepaws and Wisdom Panel, two companies I've tested on my cats.
How Does a DNA Test Kit Work?
Pet DNA tests rely on pet owners collecting cells via a cheek swab, then placing the sample in a sealed stabilizing or preserving fluid for transit. You’ll mail the sample back to the lab in the prepaid envelope. It usually takes about five weeks to get results. (The first time I sent my cat Basil’s Basepaws sample, the company emailed that the results were inconclusive, and I had to wait for another kit to be sent, re-swab him, and wait another five weeks for results.)
At the lab, the sample is analyzed against the company’s breed and genetic health database. They use single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) arrays—the standard technology for identifying breed ancestry—as well as data on inherited traits and the risk of common diseases. Essentially, different breeds have distinct patterns of SNPs in their genomes, which serve as genetic markers. These tests analyze the pet’s DNA sample for specific SNPs and then compare them to the company’s existing database to estimate the animal’s breed composition. This not only tells you about breed composition, but can also identify the specific DNA sequences that are markers for potential health risks, such as predispositions to diseases or hereditary cancers.
Don’t take the health or DNA test results as absolute truth, however. “This can lead to a false sense of security or false alarms," says veterinarian Amanda Chambers. Forward your results to your veterinarian and always follow up by scheduling a visit to the vet if your pet is marked as a carrier for any genetic disease.
What the Results Can—and Can’t—Tell You
After chatting with Richardson, I’ve found that these are the major areas of limitation with at-home DNA test kits:
- Results depend on the size/diversity of the genetic database
- Most kits test known markers only—not full genomes
- Feline data is less developed
- Misinterpretation of results can lead to unnecessary concern
Wisdom Panel claims its cat breed results are over 98 percent accurate and its dog tests are over 99 percent accurate. However, there's a huge disparity between the three kits I tested on my cats, particularly in breed ancestry. One problem with the vast disparity in results is that the three companies use different sample sizes and metrics to identify breeds.
But the biggest issue for cat owners taking these at-home DNA tests is that you can’t really identify most cats' breeds the way you can with dogs. Unless your cat is a purebred, about 95 percent of cats don’t belong to a recognized breed. Cats' genetic backgrounds are muddied—they're just similar mixes with different physical characteristics, so the tests only show the breed(s) they share the most markers with. Basically, these tests for cats aren’t able to reliably tell us about breed composition, just similarity to other breeds’ traits in the company’s data pool.
From my research, it seems the breed identification part of these tests is more accurate for dogs, as dog DNA is so much more diversified. Breeds have been clearly defined after centuries of diversification, and dog DNA mutates quickly, with genes changing after just a few generations. Cats are not much different from their Egyptian ancestors.
Interestingly, in a 2023 CBS report, the news organization sent dog and human DNA to different at-home test companies and received varying results, with the dog's DNA ranging from 65 to only 29 percent German Shepherd. The human DNA results were attributed to a bulldog, border collie, and cane corso mix.
In summation, unfortunately, there isn't a single catchall way to determine a pet's genetic makeup or ancestry. Humans like categories, and breeds are essentially human constructs based on how a dog or cat looks. The genetic part of the test is fun, but take it with a grain of salt—especially with cats.
A Note on At-Home Allergy Testing Kits
I recently tested both of my cats for allergies and intolerances using a similar at-home test kit, the 5Strands Pet Food & Environmental Intolerance Test, for $100. For this, you only need to send a fur sample in the mail to a lab; results were sent to my inbox within seven days. The report showed that both of my cats had strong intolerances to common ingredients in their diet, such as various types of fish and chicken meal. This sent me into a panic about my cats' health and (dis)comfort.
After further research, I learned that hair/fur samples are not an accurate way to measure allergies and intolerances. Studies show that kits claiming to provide these results perform no better than chance and often produce inconsistent or false results.
“There's no scientific evidence to support allergy testing through hair, fur, or saliva,” says Richardson. “Veterinarian-supervised elimination diets to test for food allergy and intradermal skin testing or blood tests to test for environmental allergies remain the gold standard.”
So, save your money and consult a vet instead if you suspect your pet is suffering from allergies or intolerances.
Meet the Experts
- Amanda Chambers is a full-time small animal general practitioner based in Kansas City, Missouri.
- Jamie Richardson is head of veterinary medicine at Small Door Veterinary.

Authorities said emergency services were called at around 2.30pm ET after the helicopter crashed in a field off Highway 10 on Saturday.
First responders said the helicopter was still on fire when they arrived at the site, located roughly 50km southeast of Montreal in Quebec province.
Audrey-Anne Bilodeau, a spokesperson for Sûreté du Québec provincial police, said the helicopter reportedly experienced difficulties before crashing in the municipality of Sainte-Brigide-d’Iberville.
The first responders found the crashed aircraft and later discovered the bodies of the four occupants. They were all declared dead at the scene.
Police said they have not yet confirmed the identities of the victims of the crash, with law enforcement still probing the cause of the incident.
Sergeant Bilodeau said the process of identification may "take a few days". He said the helicopter seems to have been a private aircraft.
Canada's transportation safety board has deployed a team for the investigation, which is being led by Sûreté du Québec’s major crimes unit.
Federal transport minister Steven MacKinnon offered his condolences in a post on social media.
"My thoughts are with everyone affected by this tragedy," he wrote.
MacKinnon said that safety of civil aviation operations is a top priority for Transport Canada, adding that the federal government was monitoring the situation and would provide necessary support.
He also announced that Transport Canada would appoint a “minister’s observer” to monitor the response, provide the minister with investigation updates, and help identify regulatory issues or safety deficiencies.

'I don't even know if my parents are alive' - the war heroes jailed 25 years ago
- Published
Hanna Petros Solomon breaks down in tears as she recalls how she and her siblings effectively became orphans 25 years ago when their father was arrested in Eritrea and jailed without trial. Their mother was subsequently detained - and no-one has heard from either of them - or of them - since.
"He had a towel on his shoulders like a sportsman," she tells the BBC about the last time she saw her father when she was 10 years old, and he had gone out for a jog.
"He used to work out every morning."
Her parents met when they both fought in the long liberation war that saw Eritrea gain independence from Ethiopia in 1993.
Her father Petros Solomon had been one of the senior leaders during the war and is regarded by many as a national hero for his critical role.
After independence, he had served as defence minister, then foreign minister and had been heading the fisheries ministry when his troubles began.
That was in May 2001 when he and 14 other high-profile politicians signed an open letter to President Isaias Afewerki calling for the implementation of a constitution that was ratified after independence and demanding national elections. They became known as the G-15.
Isaias, the leader of the Eritrean People's Liberation Front (EPLF) which had fought against Ethiopia, did not take the criticism well.
Unbeknown to Hanna, her father had been dismissed as a minister, though he still went out early to get some exercise each day.
It was not until a few days after 9/11 - when the world was distracted by the al-Qaeda attacks on the US - that the country was to discover the full extent of Isais's displeasure in what became a watershed moment in Eritrea's history.
In the early hours of 18 September, the security forces positioned themselves outside the homes of 11 senior government officials in the capital, Asmara, on the president's orders.
Petros was picked up by security agents as he left in his tracksuit.
The family had no idea what had happened to him. Hanna and her three siblings went to stay with their paternal grandmother as their mother, Aster Yohannes, was away studying in the US.
It was only some days after Petros had disappeared that things became clearer, says Hanna about the painful memories.
"My classmates told me that my father sold out his country.
"That is when I understood how serious the situation was, and how people framed my dad and his colleagues who fought for the independence of their country. I was hurt."
In the US, Aster was shell-shocked by what had happened - and was in a very bad way. She asked government officials if they could issue the children with passports - but they refused, telling her to come home.
After agonising about the situation for two years and reportedly receiving assurances from government officials, she packed her bags to return.
Hanna and her siblings desperately wanted her back - but they were also worried.
"I told her on the phone: 'What if they arrest you?'" Hanna remembers.
"She insisted nothing would happen to her, saying: 'I haven't done anything wrong, and am only coming to raise my children.'"
Hanna says she learned later that President Isaias himself had promised Aster that she would be safe. But while the family waited at Asmara International Airport on 11 December 2003, she failed to emerge through arrivals with the other passengers.
Their hopes began to wilt along with the flowers they had brought: "It was a long, long wait. Eventually we gave up and went back home.
"First we called to the US, friends and relatives told us they saw her off at the airport."
Then ominously an official called from the airport asking Aster to collect her luggage. That is when they realised she had arrived in the country but would not be coming home.
All pleas and requests for information fell on deaf ears in the months that followed. Instead Hanna's grandmother was warned by authorities to stop inquiring.
The family later heard that Aster was being held in the infamous jail known as Karshelli in the heart of Asmara.
Hanna's father is believed to be detained, with the others arrested on 18 and 19 September 2001, in the remote, hostile and highly secretive prison known as Ela-Ero, located in eastern lowlands north-east of Asmara. Accused of treason, none of them has ever been brought to trial or allowed to see their relatives.
At around the same time, the government also shut down all the fledgling independent newspapers and detained their editors and journalists - also believed to be imprisoned in Ela-Ero.
The Eritrean government - including its embassy in the UK - has not responded to the BBC's request for comment regarding the whereabouts of the prisoners or whether or not they are alive.
Hanna, like many thousands of young Eritreans fleeing conscription and in search of better opportunities, left the country - travelling secretively over the border without a passport.
Now 35 years old, she is married and lives in the US, working as a trauma specialist - but still feels traumatised herself by how she lost her parents.
As she stares at old pictures of her parents, she worries her memories will fade of the happy times before their arrest - the laughter, the family gatherings, the birthday parties: "My dad always wanted to gather people in the house, they were good days."
She also hankers after her mother's "unmatched" egg and potato sandwiches.
On trips down to the coast when her father was the minister of fisheries, Hanna remembers him organising singing competitions in the car: "He would ask us to sing one by one and whoever won would get a present."
One of his favourite songs included the lyrics: "I had a sweater, a blue sweater, that my sister took" - which reminded him of his sister who was also a freedom fighter and had been killed during the war.
She also has memories of her mother loving music - playing and singing hits by Abba, Dolly Parton and Whitney Houston.
Until her father's arrest, Hanna remembers September as being full of hope with its three big Orthodox Christian festivals, including the Geez New Year. Now the month brings her no joy.
Ibrahim Sherifo knows exactly how she feels. Both his parents, who were senior members of the ruling People's Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ), were among the G-15 people arrested 25 years ago.
He was 13 years old at the time
"For me 18 September 2001 is a dark day, but not only for me, it is a dark day for Eritrea and its people, because it is the day when law and democracy was detained," he tells the BBC.
He is now 38 and living in exile in the Netherlands, where he was granted asylum, and is pursuing an MA in political science - following in his father's footsteps.
His dad Mahmoud Ahmed Sherifo was the local government minister and de facto deputy president before his detention.
Ibrahim was with his mother, Aster Fissehatsion, staying with her sister when he remembers security agents knocking on the door early in the morning and taking her away in her pyjamas.
Worried about his father, Ibrahim immediately ran to his nearby house but was told he had already been picked up when he had gone out for exercise.
Both Hanna and Ibrahim say they are forever grateful to the friends and family who offered them care and supported them as they grew up without their parents, despite the risks.
They are also proud of what their parents stood for and daring to call for reforms.
"They had conscience and couldn't observe idly while what they fought for what had been hijacked by Isaias and his coterie," says Ibrahim.
"As a family, we should be informed whether they are alive or not," he adds, accusing the government of wanting to erase all memory of the political prisoners.
Hanna also wants the plight of the many others whose relatives have disappeared over the years to be heard too.
Sometimes it is calm and you can float, but other times the sorrow comes back to you like a wave and drowns you deep down"
Human rights groups, including the UN, consider the G-15 prisoners of conscience and have been calling for their release.
President Isaias, now 80, has still not implemented the country's first constitution - approved in 1997 - and remains in power without ever holding an election.
Hanna recalls that on the eve of her father's disappearance, she had a "bad feeling" - and had crept into his bed and tied his legs to her own with string while he slept.
"In the morning he woke up to find he was tied up and to release himself he pulled my legs and I woke up. I begged him not to leave but he assured me that he would return [after his run]."
Describing the years of sorrow since, she says it is like living in the deep sea.
"Sometimes it is calm and you can float, but other times the sorrow comes back to you like a wave and drowns you deep down.
"Sometimes you lose hope and you are out of breath."
Asked what she would say if she could get a message to her parents, she replies: "Don't worry about us.
"Like you survived the struggle through sheer steadfastness, we hope you can pull through this too and return to us."

2 Naga civilians killed by unknown armed individuals in Manipur: Police
The incident occurred just a day after four Tangkhul Naga civilians were killed at Pilong village of Kamjong district
Two Naga civilians were killed by unknown armed individuals at Kailenjang village of Manipur’s Senapati distict on Saturday just a day after four Tangkhul Naga were killed at Indo-Myanmar border district, Kamjong of Manipur, police said.
According to officers, the incident occurred at 2.45pm at Kailenjang village of Senapati district.
The deceased has been identified as Rocky from Mao Chaowainamai village and Kumar from Poumai Laii Shirafii both from Senapati district, officers said.
The incident occurred just a day after four Tangkhul Naga civilians were killed at Pilong village of Kamjong district by armed individuals allegedly by cadres across Indo-Myanmar border.
Also Read:4 bodies of Nagas found near Myanmar border in Manipur
The killing incident occurred just few hours after United Naga Council (UNC), a Naga apex body announced to lift indefinite economic blockade imposed in all national highways of Manipur with effect from 6pm of September 26.
In a statement issued by president of UNC, NG Lorho on Saturday said, “Upon the agreement arrived at in the tripartite talks held amongst the Government of Manipur, the Government of India, and the United Naga Council (UNC) in Guwahati on September 26, 2026, the council hereby announces the suspension of the ongoing economic blockade with effect from 6:00 PM of September 26, 2026. The United Naga Council appreciates the cooperation and solidarity extended by all concerned during the course of the agitation.”
UNC imposed the indefinite inter-district economic blockade in all national highways in Manipur with effect from May 17 demanding after the state government failed to fulfil their ultimatum to locate the six Nagas.
The six Nagas were allegedly abducted on May 13 by a group of Kuki individuals at Leilon Vaiphel (A Kuki village) following a twin ambush conducted at two separate incidents on the same day at Noney district and Kangpokpi district killing one Naga man and three church leaders respectively.
After the recovery of the six Naga civilians as mutilated bodies the Naga body intensified the blockade and demanded to fulfil four charter of demands including abrogation of Suspension of Operation (SoO) with Kuki militants, arrest of perpetrators, and removal of deputy chief minister Nemcha Kipgen who is the wife of Kuki National Front-Presidential faction chairman’s wife.

In West Bengal, the Bharatiya Janata Party has the support of 207 MLAs in the 294-member Assembly. Two constituencies are up for bypolls, a situation created because the elected representatives won from other constituencies in the State elections earlier this year.
Editorial | Freezing democracy: On the Election Commission of India and West Bengal
The main parties in the fray are the BJP, the Trinamool Congress, the Congress, and the Left. This is the first election in which former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee’s Trinamool will fight on the symbol of a footballer rather than its flowers-and-grass insignia.
Nandigram: a fight for prestige
The Nandigram Assembly seat, with 17 panchayats, has about 2.5 lakh people, of whom about 27% of the electorate is Muslim. This is Suvendu Adhikari’s home district.
Mr. Adhikari has stated several times that the constituency is a prestige fight for him.
The constituency
During the Vietnam War that peaked in the 1960s, West Bengal’s Left Front, powerful in the State then, protested on behalf of the country, with the slogan: “Amar naam, tomar naam, Vietnam, Vietnam [My name, your name, Vietnam, Vietnam].” In 2007, during the movement against forcible land acquisition for a chemical hub, which saw 14 people die, the Left Front government was still in power.
But this time, the same slogan went against it: it became “Amar naam, tomar naam, Nandigram, Nandigram [My name your name, Nandigram, Nandigram].”
Nandigram, a predominantly rural Assembly constituency in coastal Purba Medinipur district of West Bengal, has been synonymous with political change. The fight against forcible land acquisition brought the downfall of the Left Front government in 2011.
In 2021, when Mr. Adhikari defeated former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee by a margin of 1,956 votes in Nandigram, the constituency brought to the fore a new leader.
In 2026, he contested and won the seat by a margin of about 9,665 votes. Since he was elected from two constituencies, Nandigram and Bhabanipur, he decided to represent Bhabanipur, where he defeated Ms. Banerjee again.
Key candidates
The BJP has fielded Hasirani Rath, the mother of Mr. Adhikari’s slain personal assistant.
Ms. Hasirani has an emotional appeal because she lost her son in the post-poll violence in West Bengal this year. Her son, Chandranath Rath, was shot dead at point-blank range on May 6, just two days after the BJP came to power in the State for the first time, ending the 15-year-old Mamata Banerjee rule.
“This place has been nurtured by Suvendu Adhikari. Of course he is the only one who will win here,” Ms. Hashirani says, after she offered puja at 13 local temples in the constituency as part of her poll campaign in the last week of September.
“Most people in Nandigram have spontaneously accepted me as the daughter of Nandigram and the mother of their homes,” Ms. Hasirani says.
She insists that Adhikari will remain the leader of the people of Nandigram, and it is not victory that she is concerned about. “We want the margin of the victory to be 1.5 lakh votes,” she adds.
The Chief Minister had urged the people of Nandigram to ensure the highest-ever margin of victory in the constituency.
Former CM Banerjee initially announced her support for Sanchita Pradhan Dey, who withdrew from the contest. Then she supported the Congress nominee from Nandigram, Milan Pradhan. Within hours, he was arrested in a 19-year-old case. He was a leader and activist who was part of Nandigram’s land movement in 2007. Mr. Pradhan has been sent to judicial custody till October 3. His bail plea at the Calcutta High Court was denied on September 22.
“He has always been here at public events; why was he not arrested before? Why arrest him now when he became the Congress candidate?” Arpita, his wife, said in a video message shared by State Congress leaders.
The Left Front has fielded Communist Party of India’s Shanti Gopal Giri for the bypoll.
Key issues and campaign
In the Nandigram bypoll, the Congress is running its campaign on its candidate being arrested by the West Bengal police. “We are all Milan Pradhan. He cannot be here because he was wrongfully arrested. We are all standing here as the candidate,” a campaign member of the Congress said while asking people to vote in the party’s favour.
“Even Mamata didi has asked everyone to support our candidate,” the Congress workers tell people of Nandigram as they go from house to house. The arrest of Pradhan has brought the Congress leadership in West Bengal together and evoked a strong response from the party’s high command. Leader of Opposition in Parliament, Rahul Gandhi, called it “political revenge, the murder of democracy”.
“The BJP has no faith in fair elections — that’s why it wants to cling to power, sometimes through vote theft, sometimes through stealing governments, and sometimes through stealing parties,” Mr. Gandhi said on X.
Meanwhile, the BJP is driving its by-poll campaign on the emotional appeal of a mother who has lost her child. Mr. Adhikari accompanied Hasirani when she filed her nomination papers.
Addressing a gathering after the nomination, the Chief Minister exuded confidence by saying that the BJP will win by “such a big margin in Nandigram that no one has ever imagined”. He said that Chandranath Rath’s biggest sin was that he was his aide.
He promised to fulfil all the promises made to the people of Nandigram.
What the electorate says
Purnima, 50, from Gopalchak area in Nandigram is emotional about the mother’s loss. “A mother lost her child in these politics. We are bound to vote for her,” she says.
Amina Bibi, 65, from the Mohammadpur area says that people of Nandigram have always spoken truth to power and she does not shy away from speaking the truth now.
“I fought shoulder to shoulder with Suvendu during the Nandigram protests. But since he became CM, he has not dared to come back here because he knows he has not done anything for us,” she says. A man in his mid-50 from Mohammadpur in Nandigram who did not want to be named, says, “This is not a democracy where there is no fair election and people are not allowed to participate. In a democracy every candidate should get a fair chance to campaign and contest. That is missing here.”
Rejinagar: wall graffiti speaks
Rejinagar constituency has over 2.56 Lakh voters and about 69% of the electorate in the constituency are Muslim voters. The Bhagirathi river, a distributary of Ganga passes through the constituency, which spans over two blocks: Beldanga I and II, comprising nearly 14 panchayats. A predominately rural constituency, the region has little employment opportunities and youth migrate for work.
The constituency
Rejinagar is located less than 15 kilometres from Plassey, where a war between the East India Company and Nawab Siraj-u-Daullah of Murshidabad almost 270 years changed the history of the subcontinent forever.
The constituency, located in West Bengal’s Murshidabad district, was a highlight of the 2026 Assembly polls. Aam Janata Unnyan Party (AJUP) leader Humayun Kabir’s had attempted to construct a mosque styled on the lines of the Babri masjid in Ayodhya.
Mr. Kabir’s campaign in the 2026 Assembly polls on the issue of construction of the mosque, split the Muslim votes, polarised Hindus, and eventually was one of the reasons that led to fall of the 15-year-old Trinamool Congress government. Kabir, who was expelled from the Trinamool Congress, set up AJUP and won elections from Naoda and Rejinagar in the district. He vacated Rejinagar where his margin of victory was over 58,000 votes.
The project of construction of the Babri-style mosque next to a national highway has been stalled and the site that had hundreds of people thronging before the Assembly polls, is desolate.
The constituency had witnessed violent protests during the anti-CAA [Citizenship Amendment Act] protests in 2019. In 2024 there was an explosion during a Ram Navami procession, which left about 20 people injured.
Key candidates
The by-polls at Rejinagar have been necessitated after Humayun Kabir resigned from his Rejinagar seat on June 4. The AJUP chairperson has fielded his son Golam Nabi Azad. Neither is campaigning in a big way, saying there is intimidation by the administration, controlled by the ruling party.
The Banerjee-backed faction of the Trinamool Congress has fielded Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, a former MLA, as their candidate. Chowdhury had represented the seat for three terms, first being elected from the Congress in 2011, and later as a Trinamool Congress nominee. Chowdhury too had said he would withdraw from the contest, but later decided to reconsider, after intervention from Banerjee.
Congress fielded Abdullahil Kafi, Leader of the Opposition from the Murshidabad Zila Parishad. The Ritabrata Banerjee-led TMC faction (Democratic TMC) fielded Safiuzzaman S.K.
CPI (M) has fielded Saeed Asad Ali. The BJP is hoping for a split of minority votes and that a polarisation of Hindu votes will make way for its victory, the BJP is banking on a polarisation of Hindu votes and have fielded Sakharav Sarkar.
Key issues and campaign
The leaders of the AJUP and Banerjee-backed Trinamool Congress have alleged intimidation by the police and said that they are not being allowed to contest. Mr. Kabir has decided to stay away from the campaigning, accusing the local police of slapping fake cases against his workers and arresting them.
According to Mr. Kabir, “Fifteen of my workers have been arrested by the police, while many have fled to other places fearing the police’s constant threats. This is terrifying. Police are picking up everyone they see with me. They have become the BJP’s agents. I can’t risk my workers’ lives,” he says. The MLA was also called for questioning to Berhampore Police Station on September 21 and 23, in relation to a viral audio clip that pointed to subject matter pertaining to communal tension.
Mr. Kabir adds that his son is still visiting some areas, “But we stopped major campaigning. I will communicate with people and campaign for my son through Facebook only,” he says.
On September 19, West Bengal police arrested Saiful Islam, an independent candidate from Rejinagar, who has close associations with the AJUP leadership. While the graffiti of the Opposition candidates has come up all across the constituency, the only candidate who is actively campaigning is the BJP’s Sarkar.
While the party offices of the candidates in Opposition wear a desolate look, the party office of the BJP at Rejinagar is bustling with activity. “TMC has not done anything for this area in the last 15 years. Humayun Kabir’s corruption has also been exposed. He duped people of crores in the name of his Babri Masjid replica project. The public is not foolish. They want a change,” Sarkar says. The BJP candidate says that he is fighting this election on a development pitch and getting good response from people across communities.
While Mr. Sakharav is campaigning across the constituency, the graffiti of Opposition candidates — the hammer and sickle of CPI(M), hand of Congress, football player of Ms. Banerjee’s All India Trinamool Congress, and whistle of AJUP — are on the walls of Rejinagar.
What the electorate says
Mohsin Sheikh, who resides near Beldanga Police Station in Rejinagar, says, “The election looks very different this time. There is not much show of parties and their candidates, unlike previous elections. A strange silence has captured the area.”
There are voters who lament the lack of development in the region, health facilities, and transport. “The nearest hospital in our area is 5-6 km away. Those who stay in the part of the constituency which is connected to the national highway may still get proper transport to reach there in emergency cases. But what about the people from the other side of the river?” says Nafisa Bibi, who runs a teashop at Saktipur village, which is around 12 km from the ferry-ghat.
Hamid, a street vendor, stops at the boundary of the under-construction mosque. “It was a good initiative. When it’s completed, everybody will come to pray here from even the neighbouring districts. Our business will grow,” he says, as he prepares his jhaalmuri mix.

SpaceX’s reported efforts, in July 2026, to remove Chinese-made components from its supply chain capture a new phase in the restructuring of global production. The challenge is no longer simply where a product is assembled. It is increasingly about what lies several layers beneath the final manufacturer — and whether firms can identify, replace and verify suppliers embedded deep within complex production networks. Moving a factory may be relatively straightforward; removing an industrial ecosystem from the production process is not.
The other side of de-Sinification
Here lies a less noticed paradox. The ecosystem problem is not confined to foreign firms seeking to reduce their exposure to China. Chinese companies expanding overseas increasingly confront it from the opposite direction. While foreign firms struggle to disentangle themselves from Chinese suppliers and capabilities, Chinese firms must decide how much of the industrial ecosystem that supports their competitiveness at home can be carried abroad and how much must be recreated locally.
This difficulty is compounded by the fact that China’s industrial ecosystem is not standing still. Even as foreign firms seek to reduce their dependence on China, China is building capabilities in areas where it has historically relied heavily on foreign technology. Memory-chip maker CXMT is illustrative. It has emerged as the world’s fourth-largest producer of DRAM chips, although it continues to trail global leaders in advanced memory technologies and remains dependent on access to foreign chipmaking equipment. Attempts to reduce exposure to China are therefore taking place against a moving target: Chinese firms are simultaneously working to reduce their own external dependencies.
The reverse challenge becomes visible when Chinese manufacturers venture overseas. They too confront a form of de-Sinification, although from the opposite direction. Their internationalisation increasingly involves more than establishing final-assembly plants. The competitiveness of companies such as BYD and Xpeng rests partly on dense networks of component makers, engineering capabilities and production relationships developed within China. Moving a factory abroad therefore creates a choice: take existing suppliers along, cultivate new local suppliers, or combine the two. Each route carries different costs — and produces a different degree of genuine localisation.
Comment | Dealing with China’s weaponisation of e-supply chains
The challenge beyond factories
BYD’s expansion in Europe illustrates one response. As it builds manufacturing capacity in Hungary, the company is also developing relationships with European suppliers. Xpeng has chosen another route, contracting Canadian automotive supplier Magna to assemble its vehicles in Austria. The two approaches differ, but they expose the same underlying problem: producing outside China is easier than reproducing outside China, the ecosystem that made production in China efficient in the first place.
What makes these ecosystems difficult to unwind or reproduce is that they consist of more than identifiable suppliers. They embody accumulated relationships between firms, specialised skills, tooling and production knowledge, logistics networks, and the ability of suppliers to respond quickly when designs or production volumes change. Many of these advantages are built through repeated interaction rather than formal contracts. This is why replacing an individual Chinese supplier does not necessarily eliminate dependence on the wider Chinese production system — and why transplanting a Chinese factory abroad does not automatically transplant the capabilities surrounding it.
Seen from this perspective, de-Sinification has a less obvious, two-sided character. Foreign firms attempting to reduce their exposure to China confront the depth of China’s integration into their production networks. Chinese firms going global confront the difficulty of reproducing abroad the ecosystem on which their competitiveness depends. One side is trying to disentangle itself from an ecosystem; the other is trying to make that ecosystem portable. Both discover that changing the location of production is easier than changing the capabilities and relationships that sustain it.
What India needs to note, must build
This distinction matters particularly for India. The reorganisation of production is already creating openings. Japan’s TDK has expanded its battery production in Haryana, deepening an Indian manufacturing base that it has been developing as part of its broader China-plus-one strategy. Murata Manufacturing, another Japanese electronic-component maker, is expanding its manufacturing presence in India. These investments show that India is beginning to receive parts of production ecosystems previously concentrated in China. But making the most of this opening requires more than attracting individual factories. India needs domestic suppliers capable of meeting demanding cost, quality and delivery standards, alongside reliable logistics, skilled workers and access to critical inputs. The test is whether new investments progressively deepen linkages with Indian firms and bring specialised capabilities and intermediate production into the domestic economy. The same principle should inform Chinese investment: its value should be judged partly by the capabilities and supplier networks it develops locally. India’s opportunity is to convert the movement of factories into the gradual accumulation of an industrial ecosystem of its own.
The emerging geography of global production will therefore be shaped by more than decisions over where to locate factories. It will depend on whether the ecosystems behind those factories can be dismantled, transferred or rebuilt. De-Sinification may be visible in new factory locations and investment announcements, but its real test lies deeper within the production system. Factories can cross borders relatively quickly; industrial ecosystems, built through accumulated capabilities and relationships, are far less mobile.
G. Venkat Raman is Professor, Humanities and Social Sciences, Indian Institute of Management, Indore, Madhya Pradesh

Srinagar, Sep 22: National Conference MLA from the Baramulla constituency, Javid Hassan Baigh, on Tuesday said tourism was not solely dependent on the scenic beauty of the destination but was deeply tied to the prevailing situation of the place as well.
Talking to Greater Kashmir outside the Assembly complex, MLA Baramulla cited the example of Gulmarg, which witnessed no visitors during the period of conflict.
"Tourism is not only related to beauty, it is also related to the situation. Gulmarg is a beautiful place, but during tense situation no one visited the place. You should not link tourism to beauty," MLA Baigh told Greater Kashmir.
He said tourism is a culture that needs to be developed through a gradual process.
"I will share details of several projects for Baramulla once they materialise. When many such projects will come for Baramulla, I will share them with you. You will get an idea of where our government is and how many projects have come to Baramulla," he said.
Talking about the developmental challenges in his constituency, MLA Baramulla said Baramulla's problems are inherited, with land scarcity being the foremost hurdle.
"The problem in Baramulla is that we have inherited from the past. For example, we do not have acute scarcity of land," he said.

Otaki, Nagano Pref. – A memorial ceremony was held Sunday in the village of Otaki, Nagano Prefecture, for the victims of the eruption of Mount Ontake that occurred 12 years ago, leaving 58 people dead and five missing.
The event at Matsubara Sports Park was co-hosted by Otaki and the town of Kiso in the same prefecture. About 60 people attended, including bereaved families and local people.
Participants offered silent prayers at 11:52 a.m., the time of the eruption, and placed white chrysanthemums on the flower offering table.
Bereaved families had filed a damages lawsuit against the national government and Nagano Prefectural government, claiming that hikers were killed or injured because the Meteorological Agency failed to raise the alert level appropriately. But the Supreme Court dismissed the case in January.
The agency’s director-general attended the ceremony for the first time in 11 years and stated, “We will make constant efforts to provide more accurate information.”
Hiromi Noguchi, 68, from Azumino in Nagano Prefecture, lost her husband in the eruption.“Everyone around me has died over the 12 years, leaving me alone. I’m very lonely,” she told reporters after the ceremony.
Mount Ontake, which straddles Nagano and the neighboring prefecture of Gifu, erupted on Sept. 27, 2014. Many hikers were on the 3,067-meter mountain around lunchtime on a weekend just before the autumn leaf season. Falling cinders caused many casualties.

Africa's richest man, Ethiopia and Djibouti to build $660m fuel pipeline
- Published
Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote, Ethiopia and Djibouti have agreed to develop a $660m (£500m) petroleum pipeline and storage project linking the two countries.
The project will include a 120km- (75 mile-) pipeline connecting Djibouti's Damerjog port to a distribution facility in Dewele, Ethiopia, as well as storage capacity of about 400 million litres.
It is expected to begin operations within 18 months.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said the pipeline would reduce the time needed to transport fuel from Djibouti's port to the Ethiopian capital, Addis Ababa, from five days to one.
The first phase will transport key petroleum products, including jet fuel, diesel and petrol.
Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony, Dangote said the project would strengthen Ethiopia's energy security and make its fuel supply chain more resilient.
Landlocked Ethiopia relies heavily on Djibouti's port for imports, including petroleum products. The new infrastructure is expected to reduce pressure on existing transport systems supporting industries, including transport, aviation, agriculture and construction.
Djibouti is also expected to benefit from increased port activity, job creation and higher government revenues.
The project is part of Dangote's wider expansion of infrastructure and manufacturing businesses across Africa.
Dangote Cement has production capacity of about 55 million tonnes a year, while his oil refinery in Nigeria currently has capacity to process 700,000 barrels of crude a day and is seeking to double that to 1.4 million barrels a day.
The refinery recently listed 4.1 billion ordinary shares on the Nigerian stock exchange, aiming to raise about $1.63bn (£1.2bn).
In Kenya, the company is due to break ground next week on a proposed 700,000-barrel-a-day crude oil refinery in Lamu.

‘Tortured, kicked in chest by boyfriend’: Family alleges gang-rape after student found dead in Guwahati
The father said there were multiple injuries on his daughter’s body and alleged that she had been subjected to severe physical assault
The father of a 22-year-old Gauhati University student found dead at a homestay in Guwahati on Saturday morning alleged that his daughter was gang-raped and murdered, and demanded a thorough investigation into her death.
The student, who had gone to spend a night at a homestay on the outskirts of Guwahati with a male friend on Friday, was found dead on Saturday morning. Police arrested the man, whom they suspected to be her boyfriend.
Police said she was brought unconscious to a local health facility in the early hours of Saturday and was later referred to Gauhati Medical College and Hospital (GMCH), where doctors declared her dead.

The woman’s family alleged that she called her mother around 2am that night and told her that she was being tortured. Her father said the call was later disconnected and her phone was switched off.
“She told her mother that they were torturing her, that they would kill her, and asked her to save her. She said that the boyfriend kicked her in the chest. Soon after, her phone was switched off. Later, we saw her at the hospital when she was already dead,” the father said.
The father said there were multiple injuries on his daughter’s body and alleged that she had been subjected to severe physical assault.
“From her lips to other parts of her body and even her private parts, there were injuries. One person cannot do this. I am sure there were multiple men who raped and murdered her. We demand a proper investigation,” he said.
He also demanded punishment for those responsible. “I carried my daughter’s body to the cremation ground. She was only 22. I want her murderers to face the same,” he said.
Guwahati West deputy commissioner of police (DCP) Bolin Deori said the body was sent to GMCH for post-mortem and that the report would provide further clarity.
“As per the preliminary inquiry, this was a murder and the prime accused has been arrested. We are investigating the matter further and have detained some others for questioning,” Deori said on Sunday.
He said police found multiple injuries on the body but no blood. “We haven’t found blood on the body or the floor of the homestay when we visited. The exact cause of death is yet to be ascertained,” he said.
According to Deori, police were alerted by a local health facility after the student was brought there unconscious and responded immediately.
Police, however, have not confirmed the allegation of gang rape. HT reached out to DCP Deori and the officer-in-charge of Azara police station for further details, but they did not respond.
The family members of the accused said she had been in a relationship with him for several months and that they were aware of it. They said she had visited their home during Eid this year and was willing to marry him.
The accused’s mother said she had spoken to the woman during that visit. She said, “I told her, ‘Maa (daughter), you are an educated girl and my son is also educated. My son is a Muslim and you are a Hindu. I hope you understand what I am trying to say.’” She added that the student was aware of her boyfriend’s religion.
She said that on Friday evening, he received a call and left home. “When I asked him where he was going, he said nothing and left. Now we see that he has been accused of killing her,” she said, demanding justice for the deceased woman.
